html:
Dar es Salaam, the largest city of Tanzania, was founded in 1862 by Sultan Majid of Zanzibar as a new port on a sheltered harbour of the mainland; its name means haven of peace.

After the sultan's death it was little used until the Germans made it the capital of German East Africa in 1891 and built a railway inland. It remained the capital under British rule and after independence.

In the 1960s and 1970s it was a hub of African liberation movements, hosting FRELIMO and the ANC. Tanzania decided in 1973 to move the capital to Dodoma, a move that took decades, but Dar es Salaam is still the country's port, business centre and largest city. It is the start of the TAZARA railway, and was hit by the embassy bombing of 1998.
sum: Dar es Salaam, the largest city of Tanzania, was founded in 1862 by Sultan Majid of Zanzibar as a new port on a sheltered harbour of the mainland; its name means haven of peace.
